What the key can and cannot do

A read-only key is the standard for journals. We go one step further and check it ourselves, every time you connect.

We read

  • Your filled orders, with price, size and fee
  • Funding paid and received
  • Liquidations and auto-deleveraging
  • Fee rate and account type

We can never

  • Place, change or cancel an order
  • Transfer between accounts
  • Withdraw anything
  • Use the key from any address but 167.172.98.147

What you get once it is connected

Every number is computed from your own fills. Breakdowns appear only once there are enough trades behind them to mean something.

The record

  • Net P&L after fees and funding, win rate, profit factor, drawdown
  • Equity curve and a calendar of your days
  • Every position rebuilt from its fills, partial closes included
  • Our P&L checked against the exchange's, trade by trade

The money

  • Fees split into maker and taker, with what limit entries would save
  • Funding you paid by holding through it
  • What liquidations cost you
  • Your exact volume priced on every major exchange

Questions

Can MarginPad trade or withdraw from my account?

No. We only accept a read-only key: when you connect, we ask the exchange what the key is allowed to do and refuse it on the spot if it can trade, transfer or withdraw - before anything is stored. Hyperliquid needs no key at all, only your public wallet address.

Why should I bind the key to your IP address?

Every request we make to your exchange comes from one fixed server, 167.172.98.147. A key bound to that address does not work from anywhere else, so even a leaked key is useless to whoever has it. On Bybit an IP-bound key also does not expire after 90 days.

How is my key stored?

Encrypted with AES-GCM under a key that lives only in our server environment, bound to your account and that exchange. It is decrypted in memory only to sign a read request, and it is never sent back to any browser - not even yours.

How far back does it import?

Hyperliquid: your last 10,000 fills. Bybit: up to 180 days. Binance, OKX and Bitget: the last three months, which is what they serve. BingX: up to 90 days. Where history ends, the journal says so instead of guessing.

Does my P&L match the exchange?

Where the exchange reports realized P&L per fill (Hyperliquid, Binance) we compute our own from the fills and compare the two, trade by trade, and show any difference. A position that opened before the imported history uses the exchange figure and is marked.

What does it cost?

Nothing. No card, no trial that ends. The savings ideas include our partner links, and that is how this stays free - you see the numbers either way.

How do I disconnect?

One button on the Accounts tab removes the key and every trade we imported from it, at once. You can also delete the key on the exchange; the journal then stops syncing and tells you.

Why a journal of your real account

A demo account tells you whether an idea works. Your real account tells you what your habits cost. Most traders who lose do not lose on the idea: they lose on fees paid as taker, on funding held through, on a stop they moved, and on one liquidation that erased a week. Those costs are in your fills already. The journal reads them, puts a dollar figure on each, and shows which of them you can change.

Practising first?

Your paper trades have their own report on the My Trades tab, and the prop firm challenge tests the same discipline under a firm's rules.
